messages:
sam (eng-sre): FYI — during the EU2 maintenance window we observed a gradual GPU pool degradation. ~18m window where ~20% of GPU pods toggled NotReady and kubelet restart churned the nodes. Weighted-shift ran but some routes had a slow failover path, so customer-facing latency spiked briefly.

maya (infra): Do we have the k8s events + pod statuses? any evictions or resource-pressure logs?

sam (eng-sre): Pasted the quick snapshot from the time window:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | egrep "gpu|evicted"
dp-infer-02   0/4    CrashLoopBackOff   2   2026-08-14T09:12:03Z   10.0.3.21   eu2-gpu-03
dp-infer-07   2/4    Running            0   2026-08-14T09:10:19Z   10.0.3.28   eu2-gpu-05
Events:
  Warning  KubeletNotReady  node eu2-gpu-03 kubelet not ready after reboot
  Normal   Evicted         pod dp-infer-02 evicted: resource pressure
```
Not a single catastrophic failure, more of a rolling NotReady + kubelet backlog + delayed routing decisions.

ashwin (oncall): We saw SLO blips for 11:02-11:21 UTC. The current failover policy runs a 90s passive health-check window before shifting. That delay plus the weighted shift smoothing caused the slow mitigation. Recommend: 1) a lightweight preflight that can trigger a faster (15s) emergency shift if node-level kubelet flaps are detected, 2) reduce post-shift cache-warmup gap.

maya (infra): +1. Also propose we move the cache-warmup step into the preflight when possible. Right now we warm caches after the shift and that amplifies the latency spike. Pre-warm on candidate targets where feasible.

jordana (product): Any customer-facing incidents or tickets opened? Need to evaluate whether to proactively notify enterprise customers.

sam (eng-sre): No P0s. A handful of users reported higher latency, but no API errors. Alerting fired (latency > 2x baseline) and we paged oncall. I think a short customer note is prudent for enterprise accounts that have eu2-only affinity.

maya (infra): Proposed runbook changes (draft):
- Simplify failover checks: replace the 90s passive probe with a two-tier preflight: quick health probe (15s) + cache pre-warm, then graceful weighted shift.
- Add node-kernel/kubelet churn detector to trigger preflight automatically.
- Move cache warmup steps to preflight with a fallback to post-warm if target capacity insufficient.
- Add a short holdback window (30s) after shift to monitor cold-start errors before full cutover.

ashwin (oncall): I'll take the preflight script changes + test harness. Will iterate on the probe logic (kubelet flapping threshold).

sam (eng-sre): I'll update the routing policy docs and reduce the smoothing window for emergency shifts.

jordana (product): I'll draft a templated customer note for eu2 customers, keep it brief and technical.

ops-bot: Incident thread closed by ops-bot. Runbook draft pushed: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/infra/failover/preflight-slimdown-draft (PR #214). CI tests pending. :white_check_mark:

maya (infra): Action items (short):
- [ ] ashwin: implement preflight probe + unit tests (ETA Tue)
- [ ] sam: update routing config & smoothing defaults (ETA Tue)
- [ ] maya: add cache pre-warm step to preflight and run dry-run (ETA Wed)
- [ ] jordana: customer note template (ETA Wed)

ashwin (oncall): Scheduling a dry-run next Thursday during low traffic window. Will post play-by-play in #eng-oncall.

sam (eng-sre): Good. One more note — add cost guardrails to the preflight so we don't accidentally spin large warm pools during a false-positive. Keep warm targets small + progressive.

maya (infra): Agreed. I'll add a cost-cap param to the preflight settings and default it low for canary runs.

jordana (product): If dry-run looks good, let's roll this into the global failover sprint next week.

sam (eng-sre): Thanks all — saving these notes to the incident folder and linking the runbook PR. Will follow up after the dry-run with metrics and tweak suggestions. :thumbsup:
